question: What is the compound interest on a sum of ₹12,600 for 1(1)/(2) years at 20% p.a., if the interest is compounded halfyearly? (Nearest to a ₹)
solution:
Given:

Principal amount = Rs. 12600 

Time = 1(1)/(2) years i.e. 18 months

Rate of interest = 20%

Concept used:

Compound interest, CI = P(1 + R/100)n - P

where

P = Principal amount

R = Rate of interest per year

N = Time in years

Successive percentage of a%, b%, c% = {(a + b + c) + (ab + bc + ca)/100 + abc/100²}%

Calculation:

Since the interest is compounded half-yearly, the principal amount becomes after 18 months

⇒ 12600(1 + (20 ÷ 2)/100)⁽¹⁸ ÷ ⁶⁾

⇒ 12600(1 + 10/100)3

⇒ 16770.6

Compound interest incurred = 16770.6 - 12600 = 4170.6 ≈ Rs. 4171

**∴ The compound interest incurred is Rs. 4171.**

The interest rate half-yearly = 20 ÷ 2 = 10% = 1/10

Time = (18 ÷ 6) = 3 tenures. 

Let, P = 1000 (i.e. 10³)

C.I = 3 × 100 + 3 × 10 + 1 = 331

1000 = 12600 ₹

1 unit = 12.6 ₹

331 unit = 12.6 × 331= 4170 ₹.

∴ The compound interest incurred is Rs. 4171.
